skill.name: native-subtitle-quote-image
skill.description: Create compact 3:4 subtitle collages from authorized local or online videos. Preserve burned-in subtitles or draw reviewed scripted captions on real frames.
skill.summary: Create verified 3:4 subtitle collages from authorized local or online videos using native burned-in subtitles or reviewed scripted captions.
skill.author: chengyi-ai

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives for documented, bounded media processing, fixed update checks, normal file handling, and standard Unicode ranges. A medium residual risk remains because the YouTube recovery workflow can read browser session cookies after user authorization.

remediation.issue: The URL recovery path reads Chrome session cookies with yt-dlp.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit consent, use only the selected browser profile, never log cookie data, and stop when consent is absent.

remediation.issue: External FFmpeg and curl processes run with local or network inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep argv-based invocation, validate executable paths, enforce timeouts, and restrict inputs and outputs to user-approved locations.

remediation.issue: Downloaded media and temporary frames can contain sensitive user content.
remediation.suggestion: Use private temporary directories, clean up temporary files on failure, and clearly document output retention.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Browser Session Access
semantic_findings.description: The YouTube recovery workflow can ask yt-dlp to read Chrome session cookies for a private or verification-gated video. Authorization and no-export rules reduce risk, but a browser session remains sensitive account material.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow explicitly requests permission to read Chrome cookies and then passes them to yt-dlp. The same text prohibits exporting them, so the risk is residual sensitive access rather than demonstrated exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Turning selected video moments into readable subtitle graphics can require careful timing, cropping, and review. This skill creates compact 3:4 quote collages from authorized local videos or online sources.
actual_capabilities: Checks video tools, fonts, and optional URL dependencies before processing.
Routes work between native burned-in subtitles and reviewed scripted subtitles.
Samples candidate frames around supplied or discovered timestamps.
Renders compact 3:4 JPG collages from real video frames.
Creates contact sheets and performs per-image visual and technical checks.
Preserves existing outputs unless replacement is explicitly requested.
limitations: It does not bypass DRM, paywalls, geographic restrictions, or access controls.
Native mode cannot create subtitles when the video has no burned-in text.
Scripted subtitles require reviewed text, timestamps, and a suitable CJK font.
Low-resolution source video cannot become genuinely higher resolution.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Notes

prompt_templates.title: Make a Basic Collage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a 3:4 subtitle collage from my authorized local video. Keep the original burned-in subtitles and review every image.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: local video with clear burned-in subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Use Selected Moments
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a native subtitle collage from this video using these five timestamps. Sample nearby frames, keep the subtitle band complete, and return the checked files.

prompt_templates.title: Render Reviewed Lines
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scripted subtitle collage from this authorized video and my reviewed timestamps and lines. Label the result as scripted subtitles and check readability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: the source has no usable burned-in subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Process an Authorized URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Process this authorized video URL into a 3:4 quote collage. Check access and subtitle type first, request consent before browser-cookie recovery, then render and verify each output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: online source with possible login or bot verification.

output_examples.input: A local interview video with five reviewed timestamps and burned-in Chinese subtitles.
output_examples.output: A 3:4 JPG collage set that preserves the original subtitles, plus a contact sheet and timestamp record.

output_examples.input: A lecture video without burned-in subtitles and five reviewed lines with timestamps.
output_examples.output: A 3:4 collage with clearly labeled scripted subtitles drawn over real frames, plus a reviewable line record.

output_examples.input: An authorized YouTube link that requires an approved browser session.
output_examples.output: A consent-gated download and a checked subtitle collage, or a clear stop report when access remains unavailable.

best_practices: Confirm source rights, subtitle type, language, duration, and target image count before rendering.
Use reviewed timestamps and inspect both the contact sheet and every full-size JPG.
Keep native and scripted subtitle modes separate, and label the selected mode in delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not use native mode to translate, rewrite, OCR, or redraw burned-in subtitles.
Do not claim scripted text is original on-screen subtitle content.
Do not bypass access controls or read browser cookies without explicit user consent.

faq.question: What video sources are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports local videos and authorized online video URLs, subject to access and tool availability.

faq.question: What is native subtitle mode?
faq.answer: It crops and arranges pixels that already contain burned-in subtitles. It does not alter the subtitle text.

faq.question: What is scripted subtitle mode?
faq.answer: It draws reviewed lines onto real video frames when burned-in subtitles are unavailable or unsuitable.

faq.question: Can it improve a low-resolution video?
faq.answer: It can create a larger layout, but it cannot restore detail that is absent from the source.

faq.question: Does it download or install dependencies?
faq.answer: It checks dependencies and reports missing tools. Installation requires user approval and is not performed silently.

faq.question: How are browser cookies handled?
faq.answer: Cookie access is used only after a failed public request and explicit consent. Cookies must not be exported, logged, or stored.
